Few stop to think about the history of the mundane yet ever important device, the doorknob. Wooden doors complete with wooden handles were first used 5,000 years ago by wealthy Egyptians. However, the door as we know it appeared in the Middle Ages in the late 1500’s. Again, the door was only for the wealthy, as the poor usually only had one room homes. These doors usually featured either hand forged hinges or leather straps with a wooden bar and latch to lock the door. The modern doorknob came into being in the middle of the 19th century. Although no one knows exactly who invented it first, there were over 100 patents filed for doorknobs between 1830-1873. These started off as basic wooden door handles. Soon, glass and porcelain knobs became fashionable. Finally, the metal doorknob was introduced in 1846, rendering the other models obsolete. From then on, the doorknob has had few deviations from those early knobs, except for more advanced lock and key technology.
